activities.title: One input, two ownership models

content.title: Control vs. Freedom
content.context:
A **controlled** input gets its current value from React state:

```jsx
const [name, setName] = useState("");

<input
  value={name}
  onChange={event => setName(event.target.value)}
/>
```

An **uncontrolled** input lets the browser keep the current value internally.

The important question is not “Which one is always better?”

The useful question is:

**Who needs to own the value?**
goals: Distinguish controlled and uncontrolled component patterns and choose deliberately based on who should own the value.

content.question: If another part of the component must immediately react to every typed character, which model is usually more direct?

feedback.correct: A controlled input keeps the current value in React state, making that value available to the component's render logic.
feedback.incorrect: A controlled input keeps the current value in React state, making that value available to the component's render logic.

content.title: Why uncontrolled can still be reasonable
content.text:
A component may not need to read every keystroke.

For a small isolated input where the browser can manage the value until submission, an uncontrolled approach can be simpler.

The mistake is treating one ownership pattern as a universal law.

content.question:
Which pattern is the stronger default for each case?

**Case A:** A search box filters a visible list on every keystroke.

**Case B:** A simple one-off form field only needs to be read when the form is submitted.

options.text: Controlled for A; uncontrolled can be reasonable for B.
Uncontrolled for A; controlled is forbidden for B.

feedback.correct: Choose based on ownership and interaction needs, not ideology.
feedback.incorrect: Choose based on ownership and interaction needs, not ideology.
